evidence.label: chapter opening (sec:p15-sequential-evidence): error probabilities belong to the whole continuation-and-stopping procedure; cites Wald Part I Sections 2-4, opened at held pp.123-125 (Section 2.1 regions R_m^0, R_m^1, R_m; Section 2.3 fixed sample as a special case)

def:p15-se-model: observed information F_m = sigma(X_1,...,X_m) with trivial initial information; history likelihoods p_im, L_m and singular-ratio conventions

def:p15-se-procedure: terminal regions R_m^0, R_m^1 and continuation region R_m on histories; T the first terminal stage with {T<=m} in F_m; decision D determined by the stopped history; actual errors alpha'=P_0(Q_1), beta'=P_1(Q_0) of the procedure actually used; nontermination a separate outcome; targets distinct from actual errors; randomization seed in the initial information; the fixed sample as a special case
def:p15-se-sprt: continuation B<L_m<A and terminal regions of the selected rule; a maximum horizon or forced terminal decision is a different procedure

thm:p15-se-posterior: posterior-odds derivation of the two likelihood thresholds and their exclusivity, marked as posterior calibration rather than frequentist error; cites Section 3.1, opened at held pp.125-127 ((3.1)-(3.10))
annex:p15.se.posterior proof
def:p15-se-sprt: accept H1 if L_m>=A, accept H0 if L_m<=B, otherwise continue (equality terminates); log boundaries a, b, T, Q_1, Q_0; ratio conventions at lines 25-29
thm:p15-se-errors: boundaries A>=1/alpha and B<=beta guarantee both targets for the actual test; cites Section 3.2 (3.16)-(3.21), opened at held pp.128-129

thm:p15-se-nominal: the nominal boundaries A=(1-beta)/alpha, B=beta/(1-alpha) give only alpha'<=alpha/(1-beta), beta'<=beta/(1-alpha) and alpha'+beta'<=alpha+beta, with a Bernoulli case exceeding alpha; cites Section 3.3 (3.26)-(3.30), opened at held pp.131-132
annex:p15.se.errors proof
annex:p15.se.nominal proof
relation to the Huber robust clipped-score sequential treatment (a separate model class), as the required source extent asks

thm:p15-se-termination: geometric survival bounds under P_0 and P_1, almost-sure termination with finite mean (one-sided supports and coincident laws included); third-law termination under P(z_1!=0)>0
annex:p15.se.termination: Cauchy-Schwarz affinity, Markov bounds on {T>m}, Tonelli; k-block argument giving P(T>1+jk)<=(1-p^k)^j
thm:p15-se-errors: coupled inequalities A alpha'<=1-beta' and beta'<=B(1-alpha'), the separate bounds, the quadrilateral and the target guarantee
annex:p15.se.errors: integration over the actual first-stop regions E_m^i, disjoint over stages, identified through the proved termination; matches held pp.128-129 (3.11)-(3.21)
thm:p15-se-dependent: joint-density version under almost-sure termination; cites p.130, opened
annex:p15.se.dependent proof
thm:p15-se-nominal
annex:p15.se.nominal proof
thm:p15-se-oc: exact terminal exponential identity and operating-characteristic bounds
annex:p15.se.oc proof

thm:p15-se-deadline and thm:p15-se-truncation: termination by a horizon, and the errors of the forced-decision procedure bounded through the actual (not nominal) base errors; cites Sections 4.5-4.6 (4.63)-(4.70), opened at held pp.151-154
annex:p15.se.deadline and annex:p15.se.truncation proofs (coupling and union bound)

thm:p15-se-information and thm:p15-se-no-overshoot: information lower bounds for any terminating test, and the zero-overshoot and bounded-excess comparison; cites Section 4.7 (4.80)-(4.89), opened at held pp.154-157
annex:p15.se.information and annex:p15.se.no-overshoot proofs (finite horizon, then the truncation limit)
a maximum horizon or forced decision changes the procedure; the practical case 0<B<1<A is stated

def:p15-se-overshoot, thm:p15-se-mean, thm:p15-se-zero-drift: exact stopped-sum identity, overshoot bounds, the overshoot-neglecting approximation and the zero-drift case; cites (4.4)-(4.14), opened at held pp.142-143

thm:p15-se-oc: exact identity, bounds, and gamma-bar stated as an overshoot approximation; cites Section 3.4 (3.32)-(3.44), opened at held pp.134-136

def:p15-se-normal-saving: the source's fixed-sample comparison stated as an approximation, not a uniform 50% guarantee; cites Section 4.3 Table 1, opened at held pp.145-147

def:p15-se-transform-approximation and thm:p15-se-continuous-density: the two-root boundary approximation and the continuous density, both marked as approximations without an error bound; cites (4.36)-(4.52), opened at held pp.148-151
annex proofs of the stopped transform, the approximation algebra, and the density's normalization and moments

sec:p15-se-finite-horizons: the deadline bound; truncation changes both errors; a worked normal-horizon example separating the rigorous bound from the nominal approximation; cites Sections 4.5-4.6, opened at held pp.151-155
annex deadline and truncation proofs

thm:p15-se-repeated-fixed: each preselected look has level alpha, but the rule rejecting at the first such look has error 1-(1-alpha)^M (about .6415 at alpha=.05, M=20; one under unbounded inspection). It is compared with the first-crossing likelihood rule with A>=1/alpha, whose error is at most alpha over the entire horizon
annex:p15.se.repeated-fixed proof
the SPRT guarantee used in the comparison (cites Section 3.2, held p.129)
cumulative-look chapter: the procedure actually used is sequential, and its error is the crossing probability; the independent-look case is referred to thm:p15-se-repeated-fixed
thm:p15-w02b-p15-061-finite-error: exact first-crossing error on accumulating data, strictly above the nominal level for two or more looks
thm:p15-w02b-p15-061-unbounded: unbounded inspection rejects a true null almost surely
no constant threshold has error below one over an unbounded horizon; the SPRT supplies an unbounded-horizon guarantee via thm:p15-se-errors
warning that a valid look is not a valid procedure, and the cross-relation to the SPRT construction

defect_observations.observation: The packet's owned files (handbook/parts/p15/sequential-evidence-and-multiple-testing-w02b-p15-060.tex, its annex, intake bib and symbol csv) do not exist. The 170.1-170.4 content lives in the pre-existing host handbook/parts/p15/sequential-evidence.tex and its annex, which the packet lists as readonly; the packet also records the unit as readonly, owned by w02b-p15-045. The planned 170.x titles are not used as headings; the 170.1 material is the section 'Information, continuation and terminal decisions' (body lines 11-94). The packet's recorded sha256 for the host (872D5D6E...) is stale; the current file is F221C617...

Mirror cases are abbreviated rather than written out at annex lines 11 ('analogous null inequality'), 81 ('Repeat the preceding integration'), 195-196 ('The upper interval follows similarly'), 259-261 ('similarly gives eta'; 'Negative h reverses these two roles'), 292 ('same calculation to -X'), 295 ('By reflection it suffices'), 307 ('Reflection of the lower conditional expression gives 1/R(u)'), 418-419 ('by the same argument') and 437-438. Each omitted case mirrors, by sign or direction, a case written in full in the same proof, and the stopping and error guarantees still apply to the actual procedure, so I did not count these as unwritten owed steps. A reviewer applying the 'similarly' rule literally may want them expanded. The largest compression is the normal delta/eta symmetry and eta=1/delta at lines 295-308, which the source spends (3.60)-(3.65) on (held pp.139-140).

These source variants are not reproduced: (1) the (4.51)-(4.52) companion for B>0, A=infinity, Ez<0, with c=(Ez)log B/sigma^2 (held p.150); only the positive-drift, no-lower-boundary case is stated. (2) The derivative system (4.47)-(4.50) for conditional moments (held pp.149-150). (3) The autoregressive dependent example on p.130. (4) Tables 1-3 in full; only the alpha=beta=.05 entries are evaluated. None of these is named by the five component descriptions; noted only.

The claim that the two-root system 'is exact under zero overshoot when the stopped-transform premises hold' has no explicit annex step. It follows from thm:p15-se-transform with Z_T in {a,b} and gamma=gamma-bar, but annex lines 362-371 prove only the linear-system algebra.

The unit-level destination.lookup obligation ('Which error guarantees survive a data-dependent stopping rule?') has no dedicated lookup entry located in the handbook. It is not one of the five required components assessed here.
